thread:
Maria: Heads-up — overnight we started seeing backup restore failures for tenant-32. backup-uploader logs show KMS decrypt AccessDenied.
Kevin: can you paste the exact log line? :eyes:
Maria: ```
2026-03-20T03:14:12Z backup-uploader[pid=412] ERROR restore: failed to decrypt snapshot s-tenant32-20260320-0312: AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/backup-uploader is not authorized to use CMK arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:111111111111:key/abcd-ef01
```
Jordan: we rolled an RBAC prune yesterday that tightened S3. @Maria did that touch KMS conditions like kms:ViaService or kms:CallerAccount?
Maria: I only edited S3 bucket policy + pruned some inline role policies. I didn’t intentionally change KMS key policy. :confused:
Leo: possible grant/principal mismatch after the role rename we did last week — KMS grants bind to role ARNs, not to assumed-role session ARNs.
encops-bot: :mega: Alert: 3 restore failures in 10m for tenant-32 on s-tenant32-20260320-0312. Runbook: check CloudTrail for kms:Decrypt and kms:GenerateDataKey failures.
Kevin: triage checklist:
- lookup CloudTrail kms:Decrypt events for key abcd-ef01
- confirm caller ARNs in failing events
- inspect CMK key policy + active grants
- attempt manual canary restore with debug role
Maria: CloudTrail shows kms:Decrypt requests from arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/backup-uploader/session-abc returning AccessDenied around 03:13:xx
Jordan: that suggests either the key policy lacks the new role, or existing grants reference the old role ARN.
Leo: note: an RBAC prune job ran 2026-03-19T18:05 and removed a few inline permissions on backup-uploader. Could have removed a direct kms:Decrypt allow.
Maria: found the PR: https://git.redwood.ai/policies/infra/pull/891 — it removed an inline kms:Decrypt in favor of central CMK grants.
Kevin: if you removed inline allows expecting grants to cover access, grant propagation or principal mismatch could cause transient AccessDenied. Grants are explicit to principals.
Maria: looking at grants for key/abcd-ef01 — there is a grant but it references arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/backup-uploader-old (we renamed role to backup-uploader-v2). Ooof.
Jordan: ok root cause: role rename left grants pointing at old ARN. Remediation options:
- recreate grant for new role (fast)
- revert RBAC change to restore inline kms:Decrypt (short-term)
- update key policy to include broader principal (if acceptable)
Leo: recreate grant is lowest blast radius. @SRE-Oncall can you create grant to principal arn:aws:iam::111111111111:role/backup-uploader-v2 with operations Decrypt, GenerateDataKey and TTL 7d?
SRE-Oncall: creating grant now. Will post id. :hammer_and_wrench:
(2m later)
SRE-Oncall: grant created id=gr-0a1b2c3d expires=2026-03-27T04:00:00Z
Maria: re-triggering canary restore on s-tenant32-canary-20260320-0315
encops-bot: runbook note: KMS grant changes can take a short time to be honored due to cache; uploader should retry Decrypt AccessDenied transient failures. Our restore job lacked retries.
Kevin: opened issue to add a short retry loop on Decrypt AccessDenied in restore flow: https://git.redwood.ai/inference/restore-service/issues/412
Jordan: also add a CI/PR check that catches role renames vs CMK grant dependencies. We need automation so a role rename PR alerts infra owners to update grants.
Maria: can we query CloudTrail for similar failures in last 7d to find other affected tenants?
Leo: suggested CloudTrail query:
```
aws cloudtrail lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=Decrypt --start-time 2026-03-13T00:00:00Z
```
then filter events where errorMessage contains AccessDenied.
Maria: did that — found 7 failures across 3 tenants, all correlate with role rename/replace events in last 24h.
Kevin: mitigation plan:
- immediate: ensure CMK grants created for all renamed roles (SRE ticket underway)
- short-term: revert policy change that removed inline kms:Decrypt for backup-uploader until automation in place (PR 900)
- medium-term: add PR hook to detect IAM role renames and update CMK grants; add unit test coverage for restore flow retries
- long-term: evaluate key policy patterns that are robust to role renames (e.g., referencing trusted IAM principals or conditions), subject to security review
Jordan: recording incident timeline: RBAC prune ran, PR that removed kms:Decrypt, role rename, restore failures, grant recreation. Maria can you add to incident doc?
Maria: added timeline and draft postmortem: https://wiki.redwood.ai/incidents/2026-03-20-kms-grant-propagation-window-and-audit-proxy
SRE-Oncall: monitoring update: added alarm for kms:Decrypt AccessDenied spikes -> route to #incidents when >5 failures in 5m for same key
encops-bot: postmortem checklist recommendation: include a staging test that simulates role rename + snapshot restore, and a pre-merge scan for CMK grant dependencies.
Leo: also action to make policy-prune runs emit audit events to #eng-security with PR refs and change window so we can correlate automated changes.
Maria: follow-ups assigned:
- @Maria open PR to reinstate temporary kms:Decrypt for backup-uploader-v2 (PR 900)
- @SRE-Oncall create grants for all renamed backup/uploader roles (ticket SRE-224)
- @Kevin add retry logic to restore path (PR 412)
- @Jordan add CI check for grants (infra-ci PR 18)
- @Leo make policy-prune job emit audit events to #eng-security
Kevin: good catch everyone. No data leakage, just failed restores. :thumbsup:
Maria: resolving here; will update incident doc when PRs merge and canaries are green.
Jordan: thanks all — will close after 24h quiet window.
